The zoom keys (KTPH008KTPH000KTPH009 or KTPH010KTPH001KTPH011 with KTPH012KTPH002KTPH013 / KTPH014KTPH003KTPH015 / KTPH016KTPH004KTPH017; KTPH018KTPH005KTPH019 on macOS) zoom the terminal only while a terminal tab is selected. In a snippet editor or file editor tab they reach the editor, and KTPH020KTPH006KTPH021+KTPH022KTPH007KTPH023 types its character there.

The tab jump keys work in every tab, also while a terminal or an editor has the focus, and a number with no tab at its position does nothing. On macOS they are KTPH019KTPH000KTPH020 with a digit, and KTPH021KTPH001KTPH022+KTPH023KTPH002KTPH024 with a digit works too, so a French (AZERTY) Mac can reach its digits (macOS keeps KTPH025KTPH003KTPH026+KTPH027KTPH004KTPH028+KTPH029KTPH005KTPH030 to KTPH031KTPH006KTPH032+KTPH033KTPH007KTPH034+KTPH035KTPH008KTPH036 for screenshots). On Windows and Linux they are exactly KTPH037KTPH009KTPH038 with a digit: KTPH039KTPH010KTPH040 combinations (which arrive as KTPH041KTPH011KTPH042+KTPH043KTPH012KTPH044) and KTPH045KTPH013KTPH046+KTPH047KTPH014KTPH048+KTPH049KTPH015KTPH050 (the Cisco break sequence) still reach the terminal. A digit key that types KTPH051KTPH016KTPH052 or KTPH053KTPH017KTPH054 in your layout, such as the AZERTY 6 key, stays a zoom key instead. On Linux with a layout whose number row types other characters, the top-row digits may not jump; the numpad digits (with KTPH055KTPH018KTPH056 on) do.

Reopen Closed Tab uses KTPH017KTPH001KTPH018+KTPH019KTPH002KTPH020+KTPH021KTPH003KTPH022+KTPH023KTPH004KTPH024 because KTPH025KTPH005KTPH026+KTPH027KTPH006KTPH028+KTPH029KTPH007KTPH030 toggles the command timestamps and KTPH031KTPH008KTPH032+KTPH033KTPH009KTPH034+KTPH035KTPH010KTPH036 the session journal. On Windows, KTPH037KTPH011KTPH038 arrives as KTPH039KTPH012KTPH040+KTPH041KTPH013KTPH042, so on a layout where KTPH043KTPH014KTPH044+KTPH045KTPH015KTPH046+KTPH047KTPH016KTPH048 types a character (such as KTPH000 on US-International) that combination reopens a closed tab instead, and the character is not typed.

On Windows and Linux, KTPH004KTPH000KTPH005+KTPH006KTPH001KTPH007 to KTPH008KTPH002KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH003KTPH011 no longer reach the program in the terminal: korTTY's terminal never sent them as keys of their own, so no program loses a binding it could receive.

On Windows and Linux, KTPH015Clear BufferKTPH016 and KTPH017FindKTPH018 have no key of their own, so KTPH019KTPH000KTPH020+KTPH021KTPH001KTPH022 and KTPH023KTPH002KTPH024+KTPH025KTPH003KTPH026 stay with the programs running in the terminal. Use right-click → KTPH027Clear BufferKTPH028 or KTPH029FindKTPH030 in the terminal, or KTPH031Edit → Find…KTPH032 with the mouse. KTPH033KTPH004KTPH034+KTPH035KTPH005KTPH036+KTPH037KTPH006KTPH038 stays Terminal-only Fullscreen and KTPH039KTPH007KTPH040+KTPH041KTPH008KTPH042+KTPH043KTPH009KTPH044 still docks the file browser on the left. KTPH045KTPH010KTPH046+KTPH047KTPH011KTPH048+KTPH049KTPH012KTPH050 switches keyword highlighting and does not reach the terminal, while plain KTPH051KTPH013KTPH052+KTPH053KTPH014KTPH054 still reaches the shell as backspace.

The paste keys go through KTPH006paste protectionKTPH007: a paste with line breaks, with control characters or of a large size can open a confirmation first. In that dialog KTPH008CancelKTPH009 is the default button, so KTPH010KTPH000KTPH011, KTPH012KTPH001KTPH013 and KTPH014KTPH002KTPH015 drop the paste; click KTPH016PasteKTPH017, or press KTPH018KTPH003KTPH019 to reach it and KTPH020KTPH004KTPH021 to press it. While a paste is sent line by line (KTPH022Pause after each pasted lineKTPH023), the pane takes no other keys and KTPH024KTPH005KTPH025 stops the paste.

Every other combination of KTPH022KTPH006KTPH023, KTPH024KTPH007KTPH025 and KTPH026KTPH008KTPH027 with the arrow keys, KTPH028KTPH009KTPH029 / KTPH030KTPH010KTPH031, KTPH032KTPH011KTPH033 / KTPH034KTPH012KTPH035, KTPH036KTPH013KTPH037 / KTPH038KTPH014KTPH039 and KTPH040KTPH015KTPH041 to KTPH042KTPH016KTPH043 is sent the way xterm sends it (KTPH044KTPH017KTPH045 always toggles fullscreen), for example KTPH046KTPH018KTPH047+KTPH048KTPH019KTPH049 as KTPH000 and KTPH050KTPH020KTPH051+KTPH052KTPH021KTPH053 as KTPH001. Connections with a non-xterm terminal emulation (Wyse, TeleVideo, HP, SCO ANSI, IBM 3270/5250, PETSCII) keep sending fixed sequences without modifiers.
